findings.claim: Modal-sentence editing intensity in statements does NOT robustly track uncertainty: the full-sample correlation of per-statement edit counts (added+removed) with vix_pre28 (Pearson r=0.368, p=0.0002, n=100) is entirely 2020-driven — Spearman on the same sample is rho=0.106 (p=0.29) and excluding 2020 the Pearson correlation is r=-0.042 (p=0.69, n=90).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from results/tables/C6_edit_events.csv (238 events: 115 added, 123 removed, grouped by date) merged with vix_pre28 from results/tables/macro_by_doc.csv over the 100 statements after 2014-01-29. Mean edits/statement=2.38, max=13, 33/100 statements have zero modal-sentence edits. log1p transform gives the same picture (full r=0.261 p=0.009; excl-2020 r=-0.038 p=0.72). Top edit dates mix crisis and calm: 2020-03-23 (13 edits, VIX 50.3) and 2020-09-16 (13, VIX 26.0, framework-language revision) but also 2014-03-19 (12 edits, VIX 14.8, forward-guidance rewrite) and 2015-12-16 (11, VIX 17.4, liftoff). n_added and n_removed separately show the identical pattern (excl-2020 r=-0.057 and r=-0.024).
findings.caveats: This is a null/contradiction finding: editing spikes coincide with policy-regime rewrites (guidance changes, liftoff, framework revision), not with continuous market uncertainty. C6 only records edits to modal-bearing sentences, so zero-edit statements mean no modal-sentence edits, not no edits at all. A weak positive edit-CFNAI association (Spearman rho=0.204, p=0.053 excl-2020) is borderline and unadjusted for multiplicity.

findings.claim: Statement length volatility likewise fails the uncertainty test: |Δ n_tokens| between consecutive statements correlates with vix_pre28 at Pearson r=0.405 (p<0.0001, n=100) in the full sample but only r=0.117 (p=0.27, n=90) excluding 2020, with full-sample Spearman rho=0.131 (p=0.19); signed length change is null everywhere (full r=0.064 p=0.53).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from results/tables/B1_modal_doc_series.csv (statement rows, n_tokens first-differenced by date) merged with macro_by_doc.csv. The relationship rests on single 2020 observations: 2020-03-15 (+576 tokens, VIX 36.5) and 2020-04-29 (-197, VIX 42.4); the next-largest changes occur at low VIX (2014-10-29: -185 tokens, VIX 18.6; 2015-01-28: -171, VIX 19.0). |Δlen| vs CFNAI is null in both samples (r=0.102 full, r=0.119 excl-2020).
findings.caveats: Hazard (a) applies exactly as warned: a Pearson r=0.4 that would look publishable is an artifact of two pandemic statements. Consecutive-statement differencing drops the first statement (2014-01-29).

findings.claim: Formulaic (boilerplate) modal density per 1k document tokens is uncorrelated with VIX in every specification (full: Pearson r=-0.139 p=0.16, Spearman rho=-0.011; excl-2020: r=0.015 p=0.89), consistent with the edited-formulaicity thesis that boilerplate is inert to uncertainty; its CFNAI association is at most marginal (Spearman rho=-0.146 p=0.15 full; rho=-0.211 p=0.044 excl-2020).
findings.evidence: Recomputed by joining results/tables/modal_tokens.csv (statement rows) to results/tables/C1_statement_sentence_reuse.csv on doc_id+sent_id (formulaic = sentence key appearing in >=3 statements; join is exact for all 101 sampled statements — the 281 unmatched tokens are pre-2014 and off-cycle statements outside the C1 sample), counts normalized by B1 n_tokens. My numbers reproduce results/tables/E3_novel_formulaic_macro.csv row formulaic_per1k/vix_pre28 (r=-0.139, p=0.1645) exactly, validating the pipeline.
findings.caveats: The VIX null supports the thesis but the excl-2020 CFNAI Spearman (p=0.044) hints boilerplate density is not fully macro-inert; it would not survive BH correction across the specifications run here. Hazard (c): formulaic density has lag-1 autocorrelation, so the ~101 meetings are not independent observations.

findings.claim: Modal concentration WITHIN formulaic sentences (modal tokens per 1k words of formulaic modal-bearing sentences) is countercyclical and, unlike every other lens-4 result, SURVIVES excluding 2020: vs cfnai_ma3_lag2, full-sample Spearman rho=-0.305 (p=0.002, n=100) and excl-2020 Pearson r=-0.333 (p=0.0013) / Spearman rho=-0.374 (p=0.0003, n=91); it remains null vs VIX (full r=0.084, rho=0.001).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from C1_statement_sentence_reuse.csv (word counts of formulaic-flagged sentences per doc) and modal_tokens.csv statement rows (modal counts in those sentences), merged with macro_by_doc.csv. Mean density 39.6/1k (sd 7.0). Sign is negative in both Pearson and Spearman and in both samples, the pattern hazard (a) demands.
findings.caveats: Serious hazard-(c) exposure: this series has lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.80 (boilerplate persists across meetings), so nominal p-values badly overstate independence — effective n is far below 100 and no HAC/block correction was applied here. Also a non-preregistered, discovery-stage measure (concentration within formulaic modal sentences, not a standard density), and C1 contains only modal-bearing sentences, so the denominator excludes modal-free boilerplate. Directionally it contradicts a strict 'boilerplate is macro-inert' reading: weaker activity is associated with more modal-saturated boilerplate.

findings.claim: The existing E3 headline (novel-sentence modal density vs VIX, r=0.197, p=0.048) is fragile and should not be cited as robust: it is Pearson-only and 2020-driven — full-sample Spearman rho=0.096 (p=0.34) and excluding 2020 the Pearson correlation flips to r=-0.061 (p=0.56, n=91).
findings.evidence: Recomputed: my non-formulaic per-1k-doc-tokens density reproduces E3_novel_formulaic_macro.csv novel_per1k/vix_pre28 exactly (r=0.197, p=0.0484, n=101), then re-tested per hazard (a) with Spearman and 2020 exclusion. Note E6_subperiod_robustness.csv exists for other tables but the E3 novel-VIX cell had not been subjected to this exclusion in the correlate columns shown.
findings.caveats: This weakens, not strengthens, the paper's current lens-4 narrative: the one nominally significant novel-modality-uncertainty link in E3 is a pandemic artifact. The per-modal novel results (novel_can r=.37, novel_may r=.23) were not re-tested here and inherit the same suspicion until checked.

findings.claim: Resolving be-complements unmasks 'be appropriate' as the single most frequent predicate for three different modals — would (355 tokens), will (267), may (81) — which was invisible when 'be' (16.9% of all modal tokens; #1 head verb for would/will/may) was treated as a monolithic head verb.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from results/tables/modal_tokens.csv: 5,556/32,823 tokens (16.9%) have head_verb=='be'; resolution rate 90-94% per modal (would 2,087/2,223; will 1,330/1,454; may 462/513). 'be' is head-verb rank 1 for would (2,223), will (1,454), may (513). Top resolved complements: would -> appropriate(355), prepared(162), consistent(74); will -> appropriate(267), able(60); may -> appropriate(81), lower(18). results/tables/A2_top_following_verbs.csv (predicate-based) now lists be+appropriate at 303/231/79.
findings.caveats: A2's counts (303/231/79) are 5-15% below raw modal_tokens counts (355/267/81) and don't match any dedup scheme I tested (sentence-dedup gives 322/171/57) — A2 was evidently built on a slightly different base; cite one source consistently in the paper. 419 be-heads have be_comp_type NaN (unresolved).

findings.claim: One idiom family, '[X] MODAL be appropriate', spans a will > would > may certainty scale with a strict genre division of labor: statements commit with will (58 tokens) and use would exactly 0 times, while minutes deliberate with would (289 tokens, 74% inside reported speech).
findings.evidence: modal_tokens.csv cross-tab of be_comp=='appropriate' by modal x doc_type: will = statement 58 / minutes 74 / press_conf 113; would = statement 0 / minutes 289 / press_conf 49; may = statement 10 / minutes 42 / press_conf 22. Reported-speech share within the idiom: would .744, will .779, may .210. Dominant subject is expletive 'it' (442/726) plus rate-path nominals (increase 85, range 32, adjustment 24, firming 19). Read sentences confirm the scale: statement will = anticipated commitment ('this exceptionally low range ... will be appropriate at least as long as', 2013-01-30); minutes would = collective judgment ('participants judged that it would be appropriate to raise the target range', 2015-04-29); may = explicit contingency ('If conditions improve more rapidly than expected, it may be appropriate to raise interest rates more quickly', speech 2015-05-22). What is 'appropriate' is almost always the policy-rate path (maintain/raise/adjust the target range, pace of firming/purchases).
findings.caveats: The reported-speech flag for will partly reflects statements quoted or paraphrased inside minutes/press-conf; press_conf will (113) mixes Chair paraphrase of statement language with live answers.

findings.claim: Modal choice within the be-appropriate idiom shifts over time with the communication regime, not with VIX: will peaks in the 2013-15 threshold-forward-guidance era (102 tokens), may spikes almost solely in 2023 (51 tokens, vs <=11 in any other year), and the meeting-level hedged-modal share is uncorrelated with vix_pre28.
findings.evidence: Recomputed yearly counts (minutes+press_conf): will share of the idiom .52/.53/.52 in 2013/14/15 vs .00-.20 in 2010-12 and 2018-19; 2023 has may=43 of 79 idiom tokens (.58 may+might share). 42 of all 51 2023 may tokens contain 'extent' — the statement boilerplate 'In determining the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate...' propagating into minutes/press_conf. Meeting-level (docs with >=3 idiom tokens, n=118) hedged share (may/might/could) vs vix_pre28: Spearman rho=-0.071 p=0.446 (excl-2020: rho=-0.025 p=0.799); Pearson r=-0.108 p=0.246. Firm (will) share vs vix: rho=-0.137 p=0.140.
findings.caveats: The VIX result is a null and should be reported as one. A weak hedge-share vs cfnai_ma3_lag2 Spearman (rho=-0.221, p=0.016, n=118) appeared but is one of 8 tests run here, is Pearson-insignificant (p=.458), and meeting-level observations are autocorrelated — treat as fragile/exploratory, do not headline.

findings.claim: 'The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy...' accounts for all 46 statement tokens of would+be+prepared as one verbatim sentence repeated in every statement 2020-2026 — a clean demonstration that idiom token counts are boilerplate repetitions, not independent modal choices.
findings.evidence: modal_tokens.csv: be_comp=='prepared' & modal=='would' & doc_type=='statement' -> 46 tokens, sentence.nunique()==1, years 2020-2026, text 'The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals.' Overall would+be+prepared: minutes 99, press_conf 17, statement 46 (162 total). Similarly the 2023 may spike (L5-3) is largely one edited statement formula echoed across genres.
findings.caveats: This supports the paper's edited-formulaicity thesis but also means any time-series test on idiom counts inherits the boilerplate-persistence hazard (known hazard c); minutes tokens (99) are more varied and closer to independent.

findings.claim: A7_be_complements.csv covers only the be+complement+xcomp subset (390 of 5,137 resolved be tokens, 7.6%) and therefore understates the idioms by two orders of magnitude (it shows be+appropriate n=3 vs 726 in modal_tokens); within modal_tokens, be_comp values 'what' (141), 'percent' (42), 'one' (18), 'that' (16) are parse artifacts or bare values rather than evaluative complements, and 'able' (78) is the be-able-to ability periphrasis better treated as a quasi-modal.
findings.evidence: A7 sum(n)=390 vs 5,137 resolved be-heads in modal_tokens.csv; A7 rows with be_comp=='appropriate' total n=3 (vs 726 recomputed from modal_tokens across all modals: would 355 + will 267 + may 81 + might 31 + could 23 + can 1 + should 1 = 759 incl. might/could). Example noise: be_comp=='what' from free relatives ('difficult to know what the precise effects ... would be'); 'percent' from staff projections ('inflation would be 2.2 percent'). 'able': will 60, would 20, may 13 in modal_tokens (A7: will 44).
findings.caveats: Use A7 only for the narrow be+ADJ+to-infinitive construction (where it is clean, e.g. would+prepared 157, would+able 20); for idiom counts use modal_tokens/A2. The 'noise' entries are correct dependency parses but wrong for the evaluative-complement analysis — filter, don't blame the parser wholesale.

findings.claim: The macro correlate of FOMC modal use is uncertainty (VIX), not real activity (CFNAI): 11 of the 12 BH-significant cells (q_bh<0.05) in E1 are VIX cells, aggregate six-modal density x CFNAI is null in all four genres, and the sole CFNAI hit is a 2020 outlier artifact — the opposite of Kawamura et al. 2019, who found BoJ modality counter-cyclical vs the activity leading index.
findings.evidence: results/tables/E1_modal_macro_corr.csv: q_bh<0.05 cells = statement/vix/can (per1k q=.0017, share q=.0000), minutes/vix/can (both q=.0000), press_conf/vix/{will per1k q=.0059, will share q=.0274, would share q=.0143, could share q=.0220, can per1k q=.0000, ALL6 per1k q=.0270}, speech/vix/can per1k q=.0425, and the only CFNAI cell speech/cfnai/can per1k q=.0017. ALL6 x cfnai: statement r=-0.069 p=.49, minutes r=-0.014 p=.89, press_conf r=+0.144 p=.20, speech r=-0.096 p=.29. Recomputed speech can x CFNAI from B1+macro_by_doc: full r=-0.341 p=.0001 but rho=-0.043 p=.635; excl-2020 r=+0.076 p=.414 (sign flip).
findings.caveats: Meeting-level observations are autocorrelated (boilerplate persistence), so nominal p-values overstate independence; the claim rests on the cross-cell pattern, not any single p. Kawamura et al. used counts of an index-based modality measure for BoJ statements, so the comparison is directional, not a strict replication.

findings.claim: The single most robust cell is minutes 'can' x VIX (positive): full-sample r=+0.443/rho=+0.464, excl-2020 r=+0.445/rho=+0.443 (all p<1e-5), and the HAC coefficient on VIX (+0.0094, p=.0002 main spec) survives gaps (+0.0066, p=.0003), altlag (p=.0007), and my excl-2020 re-estimation (+0.0106, p=.0014); press_conf 'can' x VIX shows the same sign and survives excl-2020 more weakly (rho=+0.286, p=.016).
findings.evidence: E1 rows minutes/vix_pre28/can (q_bh=0.0000 both metrics); E6 excl2020 minutes/vix/can r=.445 rho=.443; E2 rows minutes,can,{main,robust+gaps,altlag}. Recomputed from B1_modal_doc_series.csv + macro_by_doc.csv: minutes can_per1k x vix_pre28 full n=99 r=+0.443 p<1e-5, rho=+0.464; excl-2020 n=91 r=+0.445 rho=+0.443; HAC(maxlags=4) excl-2020 b_vix=+0.0106 p=.0014, and cfnai flips positive excl-2020 (+0.123, p=.036, rho=+0.339 p=.001 in E6) — i.e., mildly PRO-cyclical, again contra Kawamura.
findings.caveats: Minutes 'can' is a thin series: 84 tokens over 99 docs, 56.6% of docs have zero count, max count 5 — the correlation is real in rank terms but rides on a low-count series; per1k magnitudes are tiny (b_vix=+0.009 per VIX point). Interpretation (ability/possibility talk under uncertainty) needs the token-level A-tables, not established here.

findings.claim: The statement 'can' x VIX hit — nominally the strongest statement-genre result (r=+0.370/+0.393, q_bh=.0017/.0000) — is a pure 2020 artifact: the statement corpus contains only 4 'can' tokens in 101 documents (96% zero-count docs), and excluding 2020 the correlation collapses to r=+0.006 (p=.953), rho=+0.041 (p=.701).
findings.evidence: E1 rows statement/vix_pre28/can; token sum recomputed from B1_modal_doc_series.csv: statement can total=4, zero-doc share=0.960. Recomputed excl-2020 (n=91) from B1+macro_by_doc: r=+0.006 p=.9532, rho=+0.041 p=.7013, matching E6 row excl2020/statement/vix/can (r=.006, rho=.041). Speech 'can' x VIX (E1 q=.0425) dies the same way: excl-2020 r=+0.053 p=.572.
findings.caveats: None material — this confirms known hazard (b) with exact numbers; the cell should be excluded from any headline claim despite its q_bh of effectively 0.

findings.claim: Every significant CFNAI coefficient in E2's MAIN HAC spec is 2020-driven and none survives excluding 2020, while E2's own robustness specs (robust+gaps, altlag) fail to detect this: e.g. speech can b_cfnai=-0.667 (p<1e-4 main, still -0.602 p<1e-4 with gaps) flips to +0.566 (p=.383) excl-2020, and statement will/would/could and press_conf will CFNAI coefficients all die or flip likewise.
findings.evidence: E2_hac_regressions.csv main-spec CFNAI hits: statement will -0.6471 p=.0027; statement would +0.2144 p=.0000; statement could +0.1902 p=.0000; press_conf will +0.3109 p=.0000; press_conf would +0.1711 p=.0004; press_conf can -0.1325 p=.0003; speech can -0.6671 p=.0000. Recomputed HAC(maxlags=4, density~cfnai_ma3_lag2+vix_pre28) excl-2020: speech can b_cfnai=+0.5658 p=.383; statement would b_cfnai=-0.292 p=.786; statement could b_cfnai=-0.834 p=.305; statement will b_cfnai=+1.003 p=.462; press_conf will b_cfnai=+1.824 p=.110. My full-sample re-estimates match E2 main spec to 4 decimals, confirming the same estimator. Within E2 itself, gaps already kill statement will (p=.116) and press_conf can (p=.116) CFNAI, but pass speech can — showing gap controls are not a substitute for the 2020 exclusion.
findings.caveats: Excl-2020 HAC drops 8-10 obs and creates a gap in the time index (Newey-West lags then span the gap); statement would/could robust+gaps adjR2 jump (0.04 to 0.63) is driven by corepce_gap_lag2 (p=.0000), i.e. the 2021-23 inflation era, a collinear regime effect rather than an activity-cycle effect.

findings.claim: Excluding 2020 does not just kill results — it reveals a statement-genre substitution pattern masked in the full sample: under high pre-meeting VIX, statements use less 'will' (excl-2020 r=-0.357/rho=-0.378, p<=.0005; HAC b_vix=-0.227 p=.0067) and more 'would'/'could' (r=+0.447/+0.456, rho=+0.432/+0.428, all p<1e-4; HAC b_vix=+0.137/+0.137, p<1e-4), none of which is BH-significant in the full sample (q_bh .18-.26).
findings.evidence: E6 excl2020 statement/vix rows (will r=-.357, would r=.447, could r=.456) reproduced exactly from B1+macro_by_doc; corresponding full-sample E1 rows: will per1k rho=-0.221 q=.456, would per1k rho=+0.319 q=.254, could per1k rho=+0.312 q=.254. Recomputed excl-2020 HAC: statement will b_vix=-0.2269 p=.0067, would b_vix=+0.1365 p=.0000, could b_vix=+0.1370 p=.0000 (vs full-sample b_vix insignificant: -0.062/+0.039/+0.037, p>=.33). Press conferences show the OPPOSITE will sign: press_conf will x VIX positive and excl-2020 robust (rho=+0.359 p=.0021), while press_conf could_share is negative and robust (excl-2020 r=-0.369 p=.0016); press_conf would_share weakens excl-2020 (Pearson p=.129, rho p=.034).
findings.caveats: Statement would/could are sparse series (49 and 50 tokens; ~53% zero-count docs) and boilerplate-persistent, so effective n is far below 91; the will-down/would-could-up reading fits an epistemic-hedging story but is a post-hoc subsample pattern that was NOT significant under the pre-registered full-sample BH screen — report as suggestive, not confirmatory. 2020 masks it because 2020 had extreme VIX with heavy 'will' forward-guidance boilerplate.

findings.claim: E6's '2010_2026' extension sample is vacuous: all 48 of its rows are numerically identical to E1's full-sample rows (same n=101/99/80/124, same r, p, rho) because the text series in B1 only begins in 2014 for every genre, even though macro_by_doc extends back to 2010 — so the claimed sample extension never ran on additional data.
findings.evidence: Diffed E6 sample=2010_2026 rows against E1 per1k rows: identical (e.g. 2010_2026/statement/vix/can n=101 r=.370 p=.0001 = E1 row). Recomputed per-genre date ranges: B1_modal_doc_series.csv min dates = statement 2014-01-29, minutes 2014-01-29, press_conf 2014-03-19, speech 2014-01-03; macro_by_doc.csv contains statement rows from 2010-01-27 (133 statements vs B1's 101).
findings.caveats: This is a pipeline/coverage finding, not a substantive null: the 2010-2013 texts either were never parsed into B1 or were intentionally dropped; the paper must not cite E6's 2010_2026 block as an out-of-sample check until B1 is rebuilt with pre-2014 documents.

findings.claim: The 'fair-weather' pole is real and robust: calm-era outlook boilerplate (will/would+expand, will+warrant, will+evolve, will+assess) is negatively correlated with VIX under Spearman and excluding 2020, and is uncertainty-specific (near-zero CFNAI correlation).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from results/tables/modal_tokens.csv + B1_modal_doc_series.csv (n_tokens) + macro_by_doc.csv: minutes would+expand vs vix_pre28 rho=-0.475 full (n=99), rho=-0.475 excl2020 (n=91); statement will+expand rho=-0.484/-0.459; statement will+warrant rho=-0.427/-0.415; statement will+evolve rho=-0.404/-0.391; CFNAI rho for all four is 0.07-0.14, n.s. The tokens are one recycled outlook sentence: 'The Committee expects that, with appropriate policy accommodation, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace...' (statement 2014-01-29) and 'economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant only gradual increases in the federal funds rate' (2015-12-16). Year distribution: statement will+expand exists ONLY 2014-2018; will+warrant/evolve only 2014-2018. Crucially, minutes would+expand still tracks VIX within its own active window 2014-2018: rho=-0.404 (p=.010, n=40 meetings) — the sentence was withdrawn at high-VIX meetings even within the era (statement version weaker within-era: rho=-0.315, p=.048).
findings.caveats: These constructions are era-bounded (dead after 2018), so much of the full-sample correlation is the low-VIX-era lifecycle of one boilerplate sentence; 61-66% of meetings have zero tokens, so Spearman largely measures presence/absence. Meeting-level autocorrelation from boilerplate persistence means all p-values are overstated.

findings.claim: The 'foul-weather' pole is mostly NOT stress-responsive language: could+impede and would+be+prepared are crisis-ADOPTED boilerplate whose positive VIX correlation comes entirely from the one-time 2020 adoption event; post-adoption they are literally constant (would+be+prepared = exactly 2 tokens in every single minutes 2021-2026).
findings.evidence: Full-sample rho vs vix_pre28: could+impede +0.357 (+0.409 excl2020), would+be+prepared +0.328 (+0.383 excl2020) — robust. But raw counts per minutes 2021-2026: be+prepared = [2,2,2,...,2] (43 meetings, all exactly 2); impede = 2 with occasional 3-4 in early 2021. The token is one verbatim sentence pair: 'the Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals' (minutes 2020-09-16 onward; pre-2020 the frame appears ~1x/year). WITHIN 2020-2026 the density-VIX correlation flips NEGATIVE (impede rho=-0.419 p=.002; be+prepared rho=-0.535 p<.001, n=51) — a pure denominator artifact: minutes n_tokens vs VIX rho=+0.48 in 2021-26 (longer minutes when VIX high dilute a constant numerator).
findings.caveats: This supports the paper's boilerplate-persistence thesis but contradicts reading the E5 screen's positive-VIX rows as live stress signals; the within-era negative sign should not be interpreted substantively either (it is mechanical dilution). N of adoption events is effectively 1 (COVID).

findings.claim: minutes would+be+appropriate is the genuine exception — a live policy-deliberation-intensity signal, not boilerplate: it is 'it would be appropriate to [adjust/raise/maintain/reduce policy]' deliberation that spans the entire sample, survives every robustness cut, and peaks exactly at active-policy-change meetings.
findings.evidence: rho vs vix_pre28 = +0.350 full (n=99), +0.308 excl2020 (n=91), and still positive within 2021-2026 alone (r=+0.393, p=.009; rho=+0.272, p=.077, n=43). Unlike L2-2 constructions, it appears in every year 2010-2026 (17 tokens in 2010, 43 in 2022) and only 7% of meetings have zero. Top-5 density meetings: 2020-09-16 (1.18/1k, VIX 26.0), 2022-03-16 (1.02, VIX 30.6), 2022-06-15, 2021-12-15, 2022-01-26; bottom-5 are calm 2015-2017 meetings (density 0, VIX 10-14). Quotes: 'they judged that a 25 basis point increase would be appropriate at this meeting' (2022-03-16, citing 'greater near-term uncertainty associated with Russia's invasion of Ukraine'); 'it would be appropriate over coming months for the Federal Reserve to increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS' (2020-09-16); 'all members agreed that ... it would be appropriate to make a further measured reduction' (2014-01-29). Also mildly positive with CFNAI (rho +0.234 full, +0.233 excl2020).
findings.caveats: The construction tracks policy-action intensity (tapering, liftoff, hiking cycles), which co-moves with VIX but is not identical to uncertainty; 2022's tightening drives part of the excl-2020 correlation. Autocorrelation caveat applies.

findings.claim: Several headline screen hits are pure 2020 artifacts and should be dropped: press_conf can+do collapses excluding 2020, and every CFNAI hit whose Spearman was near zero (would+be+important, will+monitor, press_conf will+need on CFNAI) evaporates.
findings.evidence: press_conf can+do vs vix_pre28: r=0.451/rho=0.251 full (n=80) but r=0.131 (p=.28)/rho=0.039 (p=.75) excl2020 (n=71); 47 of 226 tokens (21%) are in 2020 — Powell capacity rhetoric: 'In terms of what we can do... our credit facilities are wide open' (2020-04-29), 'we're determined to do what we can to get inflation back down' (2022-06-15). CFNAI artifacts (full-sample Pearson vs excl2020 Pearson, and full Spearman): minutes would+be+important r=-0.312→+0.048, rho=-0.014; statement will+monitor r=-0.276→-0.033, rho=-0.056; press_conf will+need r=-0.287→+0.116, rho=-0.021. All exactly match hazard (a): Pearson-driven results destroyed by the 2020 outlier.
findings.caveats: statement will+monitor's VIX correlation (as opposed to CFNAI) actually STRENGTHENS excl2020 (rho -0.292→-0.405), so 'monitor' belongs in the fair-weather set even though its CFNAI row is an artifact.

findings.claim: The fair/foul VIX dichotomy misses an activity-linked (CFNAI) axis inside statements: will+assess is robustly NEGATIVE with CFNAI while will+be+appropriate is robustly POSITIVE with CFNAI — an opposite-signed pair within the same modal 'will' that survives Spearman and excl2020, tied to forward-guidance phases rather than market stress.
findings.evidence: statement will+assess vs cfnai_ma3_lag2: rho=-0.353 full (n=101), rho=-0.292 excl2020 (also negative VIX: rho=-0.279/-0.246); minutes will+assess similar (rho=-0.288/-0.279). statement will+be+appropriate vs CFNAI: rho=+0.369 full, +0.291 excl2020 (Pearson +0.274/+0.324); minutes version rho=+0.331/+0.257. Both are guidance formulas: 'the Committee will assess progress—both realized and expected—toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation' (2014-2015 and again 2024-26 as 'will carefully assess incoming data'); 'the Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range... when it has seen further improvement in the labor market' (2015-03-18), threshold guidance 2012-2015 and taper guidance 2021-24.
findings.caveats: Both constructions are episodic (assess: 2013-2020 + 2024-26; be+appropriate: 2012-2015 + 2020-24), so CFNAI correlations partly reflect which business-cycle phase each guidance regime happened to occupy; with only ~2 activation episodes each, era confounding cannot be ruled out.

findings.claim: Modal-level aggregates mask opposite-signed constructions: minutes 'would' overall density is null against VIX (rho=+0.104, p=.31; excl2020 rho=-0.036) while its constructions span rho -0.475 (would+expand) to +0.383 (would+be+prepared excl2020); and the same construction reverses sign across genres (would+take: minutes rho=+0.300 full/+0.269 excl2020 vs press_conf rho=-0.298 full, fading to -0.203, p=.089, excl2020).
findings.evidence: Recomputed from B1_modal_doc_series.csv would_per1k vs macro_by_doc vix_pre28 (n=99) versus the construction-level table in L2-1/L2-2/L2-3. For the would+take reversal: minutes tokens are patience/lag deliberation ('it would take time for the full effects of monetary restraint to be realized', 2022-11-02) while press_conf tokens are heterogeneous and partly journalist speech — 14/99 tokens are in questions, 24/99 conditional ('You said... it would take a string of months of job creation of about a million', reporter, 2021-04-28).
findings.caveats: The aggregate-masking half is strong and directly motivates the construction-level lens (feedback 2.2). The would+take genre reversal is fragile: press_conf side loses significance excl2020 and its token stream mixes Chair and reporter speech, so treat it as suggestive only. Contrast case: minutes will_per1k aggregate IS significant vs VIX (rho=-0.285 full, -0.424 excl2020) even though will+continue inside it is positive (rho +0.283 full, weakening to +0.226 excl2020) — masking runs in both directions.

findings.claim: The candidate star leading indicator — minutes negated-can peaking at k=+5 vs CFNAI (r=-.576) and k=+3 vs VIX (r=+.481) — is an artifact of a series with exactly 2 tokens in 99 documents, one of which is a memorial sentence with no economic content.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from results/tables/modal_tokens.csv + B1_modal_doc_series.csv: minutes neg_can 2014+ has 2 nonzero docs / 99 (mean 0.0022 per 1k). The only tokens: minutes_20191211 ('Various participants noted that monetary policy is a blunt instrument whose effects cannot be targeted to specific communities.') and minutes_20200916 ('His absence leaves a space that cannot truly be filled.' — a tribute, not economics; the sole other minutes cannot ever is pre-window, minutes_20120620: 'workers ... cannot find full-time work'). Recomputed CCF: Spearman full-sample at k=+5 vs CFNAI rho=-.131 p=.202 (vs Pearson -.576 p<.0001); excluding 2020 the series is constant so the peak-k correlations are undefined (n≈86, all zeros). VIX k=+3: Spearman rho=+.199 p=.048, ex-2020 undefined. F2 Granger q=0.0000 both directions is the same spike: ex-2020 the series has one nonzero obs (Dec-2019) immediately preceding the COVID collapse, still yielding p=0.0000 — a single-dummy-predicts-pandemic regression, not causality. Negated can genuinely lives in press_conf (306 tokens, 74/80 docs), where its peak is reactive (F1b: k=-3, r=-.307) and F2 text->macro is ns (q=.222) while macro->text q=.034.
findings.caveats: This kills the paper's most eye-catching lead-lag number; the pipeline's only filters were std>0 and n>=20 docs, which a 2-spike series passes.

findings.claim: The F2 Granger table's strongest text->macro rows are sparse-series/2020 artifacts: statement can->CFNAI (q=0.0000) rests on 4 tokens in 101 statements (2 of them the March-2020 emergency statements) and collapses from p=.0000 to p=.456 excluding 2020; minutes can->CFNAI (p=.0001, q=.0028) collapses to p=.114.
findings.evidence: Recomputed with the pipeline's own procedure (ADF->diff, grangercausalitytests maxlag=4, min ssr_ftest p). Statement can nonzero docs from B1: 2014-12-17, 2015-01-28, 2020-03-15, 2020-03-23. Full sample p(text->macro)=0.0000, ex-2020 p=.4558. Minutes can (84 tokens, 43/99 nonzero docs; density peaks 2020-22: .176/.211/.285 per 1k vs .018-.09 elsewhere): full p=.0001 (matches F2), ex-2020 p=.1136; reverse direction .0363->.2271. Also sparse: minutes neg_will (1 token/99), statement would (49 tok, 47/101 nonzero), could (50 tok), should (38), may (27). Press_conf and minutes will/would/could series are dense (e.g. press_conf: all 80 docs nonzero for all six modals).
findings.caveats: Ex-2020 splices the series across the gap, which distorts VAR lags somewhat; but the direction of the correction (total collapse) is unambiguous.

findings.claim: After removing sparse series and 2020, exactly one Granger text->macro result survives — press_conf will_per1k -> VIX (full p=.0011, q=.0202; ex-2020 p=.0199; reverse ns p=.18) — and one lead correlation: statement will_per1k vs CFNAI at k=+3 (ex-2020 Spearman rho=.232, p=.029), whose own Granger nonetheless drops from p=.0043 to p=.154 ex-2020.
findings.evidence: Recomputed CCFs on dense series: press_conf will vs VIX k=+1: Pearson .541 -> ex-2020 .370 (p=.0016), Spearman ex-2020 .383 (p=.0011). Statement will vs CFNAI k=+3: Pearson .362 -> ex-2020 .271 (p=.0102), Spearman ex-2020 .232 (p=.0289). Granger recomputation: press_conf will->vix ex-2020 p=.0199 with macro->text p=.180; statement will->cfnai ex-2020 p=.1540. Other full-sample q<.10 text->macro rows die ex-2020: press_conf neg_will->vix .0002->.265, press_conf will+go->cfnai .0000->.465, press_conf will+take->vix .0050->.767, statement will+continue->cfnai .0084->.102.
findings.caveats: press_conf will vs VIX at k=+1 is barely a lead (next-month VIX, which overlaps VIX's own monthly persistence); boilerplate autocorrelation means meeting-level n overstates effective n; the ex-2020 Granger p=.0199 is a single un-FDR'd test.

findings.claim: 2020 does not just inflate — it flips signs: press_conf will_per1k vs CFNAI at k=+1 is Pearson r=-.406 (p=.0002) full-sample but +.320 (p=.0068) excluding 2020, with full-sample Spearman +.035 (p=.76), so the reported negative 'lead' is purely the pandemic outlier.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from B1 + macro_monthly (n=80 full, 70 ex-2020). Same pattern of collapse without sign flip: statement six_per1k vs CFNAI k=+3 (.355 -> .103, p=.34), minutes could_per1k vs VIX k=+5 (.413 -> .146, p=.18), minutes would_per1k vs CFNAI k=+5 (.321 -> .211, p=.051 Pearson, .162 ns Spearman), statement six_per1k vs VIX k=+6 (-.363 -> -.149, p=.17). F1b (results/tables/F1b_ccf_peaks.csv) reports only full-sample Pearson.
findings.caveats: None material; this validates the known hazard (a) for the F-lens specifically.

findings.claim: The dominant robust direction is macro -> text (language reacting), not text -> macro: the single largest CCF in F1b is macro leading text (minutes will+assess vs VIX at k=-7, r=-.608), and the F2 rows that survive FDR at q<.05 in the macro->text direction on dense series include minutes can<-VIX (q=0.0000), statement could<-CFNAI (q=0.0000), minutes could+impede<-CFNAI (q=0.0000), press_conf will+need<-VIX (q=.0022), minutes would+continue<-VIX (q=.011), minutes would+be+appropriate<-CFNAI (q=.0126); press_conf neg_will vs VIX, bidirectional in the full sample (q=.0044/.0165), resolves ex-2020 to macro->text only (p=.0007 vs text->macro p=.265).
findings.evidence: F1b_ccf_peaks.csv row 1 and F2_granger.csv q columns, read directly; press_conf neg_will ex-2020 Granger recomputed (n=71, p_text_to_macro=.2650, p_macro_to_text=.0007). Press_conf neg_will is dense (217 tokens, 67/80 docs), so this is not a sparsity artifact.
findings.caveats: Some macro->text rows involve semi-sparse series (statement could: 50 tokens/101 docs; minutes can: 84 tokens) and were not all individually re-run ex-2020; the qualitative asymmetry (many reverse-direction survivors vs one forward survivor) is what carries the claim.

findings.claim: F3 establishes no incremental predictive power: 0 of 113 rows pass q<.10 (minimum q_bh=.462), so the paper must state that no modal feature adds predictive power over CFNAI+VIX persistence after multiplicity control.
findings.evidence: results/tables/F3_predictive.csv read directly: best pre-FDR row is minutes would+expand -> dVIX(+28d), b=-4.359, p=.0042, but d_adjR2=.005 (adjR2 .033->.038), q=.462; second best statement will_per1k -> CFNAI_MA3(+3m), b=.126, p=.0464, d_adjR2=.127 (adjR2 -.010->.117), q=.5452; largest d_adjR2 overall is press_conf will_per1k -> dVIX, .154, but p=.0716, q=.5452. All remaining 110 rows have q>=.5452. Note the base models themselves have near-zero adjR2 (statement base -.010 to -.002), so even the .127 gain is on an unpredictable target with a p-value that dies under FDR.
findings.caveats: F3 targets (CFNAI+3m, 28-day dVIX) are only two of many horizons; honest phrasing is 'not established at these horizons', but the consonant statement-will lead correlation (L3-3) gives at most suggestive, not predictive, status.

verdicts.recomputation: All claim numbers reproduce exactly from B1_modal_doc_series.csv + macro_by_doc.csv (n=101 statements): full-sample Pearson r=+0.370 (p=.0001), Spearman rho=+0.182 (p=.0679) — the +0.393 in E1 is the share-basis Pearson; token sum 'can'=4, zero-doc share=0.9604. Excl-2020 (n=91): r=+0.006 (p=.9532), rho=+0.041 (p=.7013), matching E6 row excl2020/statement/vix_pre28/can exactly. Subperiod sign check: 2014-2019 (n=48, 2 tokens) r=+0.140 (p=.344) n.s.; 2021-2026 (n=43) has ZERO 'can' tokens — zero-variance series, correlation undefined. The 4 nonzero docs are 2014-12-17, 2015-01-28, and the two March 2020 emergency statements with VIX pre-28 of 36.5 and 50.3 — these two 2020 outliers alone drive the Pearson. Speech 'can' x VIX also verified: full r=+0.251 (p=.0049) collapses to r=+0.053 (p=.5716), rho=+0.064 (p=.4938) excl-2020. Per the rubric the underlying effect is an outlier artifact (fails excl-2020, hazard (b) sparse series with 96% zero docs, hazard (a) 2020 outlier); the candidate finding asserting exactly this is therefore confirmed, with one detail even stronger than claimed: the post-2020 statement corpus contains no 'can' tokens at all.
verdicts.revised_claim: The nominally strongest statement-genre cell, 'can' x VIX (r=+0.370 per1k / +0.393 share, q_bh<=.0017), is a pure 2020 outlier artifact and is excluded from all headline claims: the statement corpus contains only 4 'can' tokens across 101 documents (96.0% zero-count), two of which occur in the March 2020 emergency statements when pre-meeting VIX was 36.5 and 50.3; excluding 2020 the correlation vanishes (r=+0.006, p=.953; rho=+0.041, p=.701; n=91), the full-sample Spearman was never significant (rho=+0.182, p=.068), and the 2021-2026 statements contain zero 'can' tokens. The speech 'can' x VIX cell (E1 q=.0425) fails identically (excl-2020 r=+0.053, p=.572).

verdicts.recomputation: All headline numbers reproduce exactly from B1_modal_doc_series.csv + macro_by_doc.csv (statement genre, per1k vs vix_pre28). Full sample (n=101): will r=-0.116/rho=-0.221, would r=+0.176/rho=+0.319, could r=+0.177/rho=+0.312 — matches E1. Excl-2020 (n=91): will r=-0.357 p=.0005, rho=-0.378 p=.0002, HAC b_vix=-0.2269 p=.0067; would r=+0.447, rho=+0.432, HAC b_vix=+0.1365 p<1e-4; could r=+0.456, rho=+0.428, HAC b_vix=+0.1370 p<1e-4 — all match the claim. BUT the required subperiod sign-consistency check kills the would/could half: within 2014-2019 (n=48) would r=-0.167, could r=-0.117; within 2021-2026 (n=43) would r=-0.086, could r=-0.027 — the positive sign flips to negative (or zero) in BOTH halves. Mechanism confirmed as Simpson's paradox / era composition: pre-2020 statements contain essentially no would/could (1 and 4 tokens, 92-98% zero docs; means 0.04/0.10 per1k) vs post-2021 (45/43 tokens, 0% zeros; means 2.74/2.64 per1k), and mean vix_pre28 is higher post-2021 (19.5 vs 14.9). Adding an era dummy (post-2021) to the excl-2020 HAC regression collapses would b_vix to -0.010 (p=.188) and could b_vix to +0.0006 (p=.950), with the era dummy absorbing everything (b_era=+2.7/+2.6, p<1e-4). The will half fully survives every check: same negative sign in both halves (2014-19 r=-0.379 p=.008, HAC b_vix=-0.328 p=.033; 2021-26 r=-0.348 p=.022, HAC b_vix=-0.149 p=.041), zero-share 0%, 547 tokens, and it STRENGTHENS with the era dummy (b_vix=-0.250, p=.0024).
verdicts.revised_claim: Excluding 2020 reveals a robust negative statement-genre 'will' x pre-meeting-VIX association masked by the pandemic outlier: under high pre-meeting VIX, statements use less 'will' (excl-2020 r=-0.357, rho=-0.378, p<=.0005; HAC b_vix=-0.227, p=.0067), with the same sign and p<.05 in both the 2014-2019 and 2021-2026 halves and robustness to an era dummy (b_vix=-0.250, p=.0024) — though it was not BH-significant under the pre-registered full-sample screen and should be reported as suggestive. The apparent compensating rise in 'would'/'could' (excl-2020 r=+0.45) must NOT be reported as a substitution effect: it is a Simpson's-paradox artifact of era composition — pre-2020 statements contain almost no would/could tokens (1 and 4) while post-2021 statements use them routinely under higher average VIX, and controlling for a post-2021 dummy eliminates the VIX coefficient entirely (would p=.19, could p=.95), with the sign negative within both subperiods.

verdicts.recomputation: Minutes can_per1k x vix_pre28: full n=99 r=+0.4432 (p=4.3e-06), rho=+0.4643 (p=1.3e-06); excl-2020 n=91 r=+0.4451 (p=9.9e-06), rho=+0.4426 (p=1.1e-05) — matches claimed +0.443/+0.464 and +0.445/+0.443 exactly. HAC(maxlags=4) minutes: full b_vix=+0.00943 p=0.00024 (matches E2 main +0.0094/p=.0002); excl-2020 b_vix=+0.01060 p=0.00141 (matches claimed +0.0106/p=.0014); E2 rows verified verbatim (gaps +0.0066 p=.0003; altlag +0.0093 p=.0007). CFNAI excl-2020 flips positive as claimed: r=+0.311 p=.0027, rho=+0.339 p=.0010; HAC b_cfnai=+0.123 p=.036. Zero-share check: 84 tokens, 56.6% zero docs, max 5 — thin as caveated, but not a denominator artifact: raw count rho=+0.439, binary any-can indicator rho=+0.427 (p=2.4e-05), and median VIX is 18.9 in can>0 docs vs 14.4 in zero docs (MWU p=2.6e-05). Subperiod sign check (minutes): 2014-2019 r=+0.054 (p=.72), rho=+0.228 (p=.12); 2021-2026 r=+0.626, rho=+0.623 (p<1e-5) — sign consistent in both halves but the pre-2020 half alone is not significant, so the pooled correlation is partly a cross-period level effect. Press_conf: full r=+0.454/rho=+0.408; excl-2020 r=+0.242 p=.042, rho=+0.286 p=.016 (matches claim), BUT within-half signs are r=-0.097 (2014-19) and r=+0.113 (2021-26), both null — the press_conf echo is entirely a between-period contrast and should be downgraded further than "more weakly".
verdicts.revised_claim: The single most robust cell is minutes 'can' x VIX (positive): full-sample r=+0.443/rho=+0.464, excl-2020 r=+0.445/rho=+0.443 (all p<1e-4), and the HAC VIX coefficient (+0.0094, p=.0002 main spec) survives gaps (+0.0066, p=.0003), altlag (+0.0093, p=.0007), and excl-2020 re-estimation (+0.0106, p=.0014); the effect is not a document-length or zero-inflation artifact (raw-count rho=+0.44; the binary any-'can' indicator alone gives rho=+0.43, and median pre-meeting VIX is 18.9 in minutes containing 'can' vs 14.4 in those without). Excl-2020 CFNAI turns mildly pro-cyclical (r=+0.31, rho=+0.34, HAC +0.12 p=.036). Caveats: the series is thin (84 tokens, 57% zero docs, max 5) and the positive sign, while consistent in both halves, is significant only post-2021 (2014-19 rho=+0.23, p=.12; 2021-26 rho=+0.62, p<1e-5), so part of the pooled correlation is a cross-period level shift. The press_conf 'can' x VIX echo survives excl-2020 (rho=+0.286, p=.016) but shows no within-half association in either 2014-19 or 2021-26 and should be treated as suggestive only.

verdicts.recomputation: (1) Core statistic: merged all 48 E6 sample=2010_2026 rows with E1 per1k rows on (genre, macro, modal, metric) — every column (n, r, p, rho, p_rho) is identical in all 48 rows (e.g. statement/vix_pre28/can: n=101, r=0.370, p=0.0001, rho=0.182 in both). Coverage: B1_modal_doc_series min dates are statement 2014-01-29, minutes 2014-01-29, press_conf 2014-03-19, speech 2014-01-03 (n=101/99/80/124), while macro_by_doc extends to 2010-01-27 (statement 133 rows, 127 total pre-2014 rows) and ZERO pre-2014 macro rows match any B1 doc_id — so a >=2010 filter adds no observations. Recomputing correlations from raw B1+macro with date>=2010 reproduces E1 exactly (statement/vix/can n=101 r=0.370 p=0.0001; statement/cfnai/will n=101 r=-0.222 p=0.0258; speech/vix/would n=124 r=-0.113), proving the "extension" ran on the same 2014-2026 data. (2) Excl-2020: E6's excl2020 block is genuinely different (statement/vix/can drops to n=91 r=0.006 p=0.95), so only the 2010_2026 block is vacuous, not the table's mechanism. (3) Spearman matches E1 identically in all 48 rows too. (4) Zero-share check on the example cell: statement 'can' is zero in 96.0% of docs (4 tokens total), and its full-sample r=0.370 collapses to r=0.006 excl-2020 with 2021-26 half undefined (constant zeros) — an outlier/sparsity artifact, reinforcing that this block must not be cited. (5) Subperiod signs are irrelevant to the pipeline claim but were run for the examples; the identity result does not depend on them.
verdicts.revised_claim: E6's "2010_2026" sample is not an out-of-sample extension: all 48 of its rows are numerically identical (same n=101/99/80/124, r, p, rho, p_rho) to E1's full-sample per1k rows, because the parsed text series in B1_modal_doc_series.csv begins only in 2014 for every genre (statement/minutes 2014-01-29, press_conf 2014-03-19, speech 2014-01-03) while macro_by_doc.csv extends back to 2010-01-27 with 127 pre-2014 rows that match no B1 document. The paper must not cite E6's 2010_2026 block as a sample-extension or out-of-sample robustness check; it should either be dropped from E6 or B1 must be rebuilt with the 2010-2013 documents before that label is used. (E6's excl2020 block is unaffected and remains valid.)

verdicts.recomputation: Full-sample HAC(maxlags=4) re-estimates match E2 main spec to 4 decimals for all 7 CFNAI hits. Excl-2020 (n drops 101→91 statements, 80→71 press_conf, 124→118 speeches): all 7 lose significance at 5% and 5 of 7 FLIP SIGN — statement will -0.6471 (p=.0027)→+1.0027 (p=.462); statement would +0.2144 (p<1e-4)→-0.2921 (p=.786); statement could +0.1902 (p<1e-4)→-0.8341 (p=.305); press_conf can -0.1325 (p=.0003)→+0.3933 (p=.306); speech can -0.6671 (p<1e-4)→+0.5658 (p=.383); press_conf will keeps sign +0.3109→+1.8241 but p=.110 (its excl-2020 Pearson r=.312 p=.008 is the one borderline survivor); press_conf would keeps sign +0.1711→+0.2786, p=.625. Spearman: full-sample rho is already null for ALL seven (|rho|≤.163, all p>.14; speech can rho=-.043 p=.635 vs Pearson r=-.341) — significance is pure 2020 Pearson leverage; excl-2020 Spearman all null except statement could rho=-.186 p=.077 with sign OPPOSITE the main-spec coefficient. Zero-share check: statement would 53.5% and statement could 50.5% zero meetings (sparse-series artifacts); speech can 10.5%, others 0%. Subperiod signs: no hit is sign-consistent across 2014-19 vs 2021-26; three flip to significant OPPOSITE-sign effects in 2021-26 (statement could -0.99 p<1e-4; press_conf will +2.56 p=.035; speech can +0.95 p=.024). E2's internal rows verified as quoted: robust+gaps keeps speech can (-0.6018, p<1e-4) while pushing statement will and press_conf can to p=.116; statement would/could robust+gaps adjR2 0.629/0.621 is carried by corepce_gap_lag2 p=.0000. E6 excl2020 correlation rows corroborate (all CFNAI r and rho non-significant except none).
verdicts.revised_claim: The apparent CFNAI-activity effects in E2's main HAC spec are 2020 pandemic-outlier artifacts, not activity-cycle effects: all seven significant main-spec CFNAI coefficients (statement will/would/could, press_conf will/would/can, speech can) lose significance when 2020 is excluded, five of seven flip sign, and full-sample Spearman correlations are already null for every one (|rho|<=.16), confirming pure Pearson leverage from the 2020 CFNAI/VIX extremes; the one partial exception is press_conf will, which retains a positive sign excl-2020 (HAC p=.11; Pearson r=.31, p=.008) and so is at most suggestive rather than dead. E2's own robustness specs do not substitute for the 2020 exclusion: robust+gaps still passes speech can (b=-0.60, p<1e-4), altlag passes six of seven, and the statement would/could robust+gaps adjR2 jump to ~0.62 is driven by corepce_gap_lag2 (the 2021-23 inflation regime), not CFNAI. Additionally, the statement would and could series are >50% zero meetings, so their time-series tests are unreliable regardless. CFNAI results from E2's main spec should not be reported as findings; only 2020-excluded, rank-robust estimates qualify.

verdicts.recomputation: E1 verified exactly: 12 q_bh<.05 cells = 11 VIX + 1 CFNAI (speech/can/per1k), all listed q-values match. Recomputed from B1_modal_doc_series + macro_by_doc (n docs match E1). (1) Sole CFNAI hit, speech can_per1k x cfnai_ma3_lag2: full r=-0.341 p=.0001 but rho=-0.043 p_rho=.635; (2) excl-2020 r=+0.076 p=.414 (SIGN FLIP), rho=+0.056; (5) halves both positive nonsig (2014-19 r=+0.012, 2021-26 r=+0.216) — a pure 2020-outlier Pearson artifact; (4) not a zero-series artifact: only 10.5% of speeches have zero 'can', median count 3. ALL6 x CFNAI full-sample null in all four genres (statement r=-.069 p=.49, minutes r=-.014 p=.89, press_conf r=+.144 p=.20, speech r=-.096 p=.29 — matches evidence), and excl-2020 no genre shows a NEGATIVE (counter-cyclical) relation; press_conf turns significantly POSITIVE excl-2020 (r=+.355 p=.0024, rho=+.285 p=.016; HAC Newey-West coef +2.94 p=.019 controlling VIX) — pro-cyclical, i.e. still opposite to Kawamura. Adversarial check of the VIX side: 3 of 11 VIX cells are themselves 2020 artifacts (statement/can per1k & share: excl-2020 r=.006/.014, rho=.041; speech/can: excl-2020 r=.053), and press_conf would_share weakens (excl-2020 Pearson p=.13, rho p=.034); but the remaining cells survive excl-2020 with same sign and p<.05 — minutes/can r=.445 rho=.443 p<1e-5 (driven by 2021-26 half: r=.626 vs .054 in 2014-19), press_conf will per1k r=.319 p=.007, can per1k r=.242 p=.042, could_share r=-.369 p=.0016, ALL6 per1k rho=.254 p=.033 — with consistent signs across both halves.
verdicts.revised_claim: The macro correlate of FOMC modal use is uncertainty (VIX), not real activity (CFNAI): 11 of the 12 BH-significant cells (q_bh<.05) in E1 are VIX cells, and the sole CFNAI hit (speech x can, r=-.34) is a 2020 outlier artifact — Spearman rho=-.04 (p=.64) and the sign flips to +.08 when 2020 is excluded. No genre shows a counter-cyclical relation between aggregate six-modal density and CFNAI in the full sample or excluding 2020 — the opposite of Kawamura et al. (2019), who found BoJ statement modality counter-cyclical vs the activity leading index (a directional contrast, not a strict replication; and note press-conference density is if anything mildly PRO-cyclical once 2020 is excluded, r=+.36, further contradicting counter-cyclicality). The robust VIX evidence concentrates in minutes (can: r≈.44, Spearman-confirmed, excl-2020 stable, though driven mainly by 2021-26) and press conferences (will+, can+, could-, aggregate+; excl-2020 stable); the statement/can and speech/can VIX cells are themselves 2020-driven and should not be cited as independent support.
